AN1.claim: The islands recorded 0.71 million domestic tourist visits in 2024, more than double 2023, and about 11,000 foreign visits.

AN2.claim: Most foreign visitors no longer need a Restricted Area Permit for the 29 islands removed from the RAP regime; 11 more are RAP-free for day visits until 31 December 2027. Citizens of Afghanistan, China and Pakistan, and people of those origins, still need a RAP approved in advance.

evidence.quote: The foreign nationals are not required to obtain a Restricted Area Permit (RAP) for visiting the 29 islands in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands that have been excluded from the RAP regime.
Additionally, 11 islands have been exempted from the RAP requirement for day visits only, and this exemption is valid up to 31/12/2027.
However, this relaxation is not applicable to nationals belonging to the Prior Reference Category (PRC) countries, namely Afghanistan, China (including Hong Kong and Macau), and Pakistan.

AN3.claim: Reserved forests, wildlife sanctuaries and tribal reserves need separate approvals, and RAP applications are made online through the FRRO portal.

evidence.quote: Separate approvals from the competent authority shall continue to be required for visiting Reserved Forests, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Tribal Reserves.
Applications for RAP may be submitted online at https://indianfrro.gov.in

AN4.claim: The Jarawa, a protected tribe of South and Middle Andaman, shun outside contact; any attempt to interact with them is illegal.

evidence.quote: Any attempt to interact with the isolated tribe, who themselves shun contact with outsiders, is deemed illegal.

AN5.claim: Temperatures stay around 23–31 °C all year; rain comes with the monsoons, and tropical cyclones are common in late summer.

evidence.quote: the average ranging from 23 to 31 °C (73 to 88 °F)
The rainfall is dependent on the monsoons and tropical cyclones are common in late summer.

AN6.claim: Incredible India makes the case for the monsoon (late May to end July): greener landscapes, fewer visitors and hotel discounts.

evidence.quote: Come monsoons (between late May to end July)

AN7.claim: Barren Island, about 135 km from Sri Vijaya Puram, is India's only active volcano; it can be seen only from a boat.

AN8.claim: Commercial fishing is banned in Andaman waters to protect dugongs, giant sea turtles and corals.

evidence.quote: commercial fishing in the waters surrounding the Andaman Islands is banned

AN9.claim: Bengali is the most widely spoken language, followed by Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam.

evidence.quote: Bengali is the most dominant language, followed by Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam.

overview.text:
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal, about 1,190 km from Chennai. Visitors come for coral reefs and white-sand beaches — Radhanagar on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock) above all — and for the history of the capital, Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), where the Cellular Jail recalls India's freedom struggle. Domestic tourist visits more than doubled in 2024, to 0.71 million.

The islands are also fragile. Commercial fishing is banned to protect dugongs, turtles and corals, the Jarawa tribe's reserve is closed to contact, and Barren Island — India's only active volcano — can be seen only from a boat. Bengali is the most widely spoken language.

best_time.text: Temperatures stay around 23–31 °C year-round. Rain comes with the monsoons, and tropical cyclones are common in late summer. Incredible India makes the case for monsoon travel (late May to end July): greener islands, fewer visitors and hotel discounts.

how_to_reach.text: Veer Savarkar International Airport in Sri Vijaya Puram is the main gateway; the capital is about 1,190 km from Chennai and 1,255 km from Kolkata. Between islands, government ferries and private catamarans link Sri Vijaya Puram with Swaraj and Shaheed Dweep.

overview.text:
Sri Vijaya Puram — called Port Blair until 13 September 2024 — is the capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the gateway for most visitors, via Veer Savarkar International Airport. Its history is heavy: the Cellular Jail held freedom fighters in solitary confinement, and from 1943 to 1944 the town was headquarters of Subhas Chandra Bose's Azad Hind government.

Today it is a base for exploring. A short ferry ride takes you to the ruins of Ross Island, renamed Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island, or to North Bay's reefs and underwater sea walks. Corbyn's Cove is a palm-fringed beach a few km south, and Chidiya Tapu, about 28 km away, is the place for birdwatching and sunsets. The Anthropological Museum introduces the islands' tribes.

items.body: Grilled lobster basted with butter and herbs.
Fish curry with coconut milk and tamarind.
Barbecued prawns and squid fry.
See the Cellular Jail and its evening light and sound show.
Take the ferry to Ross Island's ruins.
Snorkel or try an underwater sea walk at North Bay.
Watch the sunset at Chidiya Tapu.
Visit the Anthropological and Samudrika museums.

items.title: Visas
items.body: Apply for an e-Tourist visa at least 4 days before arrival; your passport needs at least six months' validity.

items.title: Payments
items.body: Visitors can pay by QR code with NPCI's UPI One World wallet after a passport-and-visa KYC check. Carry some cash for small purchases.

items.body: Dial 112 for police, fire or ambulance.

places.name: Cellular Jail National Memorial
places.summary: The colonial prison known as Kala Pani, now a National Memorial with an evening light and sound show.
places.seoTitle: Cellular Jail, Sri Vijaya Puram: History & Show Timings
places.seoDescription: Visit the Cellular Jail National Memorial in Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair): its history as Kala Pani, the surviving wings, and light and sound show timings.

images.commons: File:Front View of Cellular Jail, Port Blair.JPG
images.alt: The cream-coloured twin-towered entrance of the Cellular Jail National Memorial
images.caption: Cellular Jail National Memorial

overview.text:
The Cellular Jail — 'Kala Pani', the black waters — was built between 1896 and 1906 to hold political prisoners in solitary confinement. Seven wings radiated from a central watchtower like the spokes of a wheel, with 696 cells; today only the tower and three wings remain. Prisoners who protested the conditions went on hunger strike and were often force-fed.

It is now a National Memorial; V. D. Savarkar was among its best-known prisoners. Walk the corridors and cells, then stay for the evening light and sound show.

items.body: The central watchtower, from which guards could see every wing.
The tiny solitary cells, each with a single high ventilator.
The surviving three wings of the original seven.
The evening light and sound show.

items.title: Light and sound show
items.body: Hindi 5:50 pm daily; English 6:50 pm on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays (Incredible India listing).

places.name: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island (Ross Island)
places.summary: The ruined former British headquarters, a short boat ride from the capital.
places.seoTitle: Ross Island (Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island): Ruins & Show
places.seoDescription: Visit Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island (Ross Island) from Sri Vijaya Puram: British-era ruins, Japanese bunkers, two museums and the evening sound and light show.

images.commons: File:Ruins of British colonial building overgrown with roots, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island aka Ross Island, Andaman vrvbaan042k24 (32).jpg
images.alt: Tree roots growing over the brick walls of a ruined British building on Ross Island
images.caption: Ruins on Ross Island

overview.text:
A short boat ride from Sri Vijaya Puram, this small island was the British administrative headquarters until an earthquake struck in 1941. In World War II it was occupied by Japan. In December 2018 it was renamed Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island.

Today tree roots grip the ruins of the Chief Commissioner's House and the Presbyterian Church. You can step into Japanese bunkers and visit two museums, the Ross Island Museum and the Smritika Museum. A sound and light show runs at 5:30 pm every day except Wednesday.

items.body: Ruins of the church, bakery, tennis court and swimming pool.
The Chief Commissioner's House and Presbyterian Church.
Japanese bunkers from World War II.
The memorial to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
The deer park.

places.name: Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island)
places.summary: Home of Radhanagar Beach and the islands' best diving and snorkelling.
places.seoDescription: Plan a trip to Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island): Radhanagar Beach, Elephant Beach snorkelling, diving, kayaking, sea walks and ferries from Sri Vijaya Puram.

images.commons: File:Havelock Island, Radhanagar Beach before sunset, Andaman Islands.jpg
images.alt: The long sweep of Radhanagar Beach with forest behind, Swaraj Dweep
images.caption: Radhanagar Beach, Swaraj Dweep

overview.text:
Swaraj Dweep, formerly Havelock Island, is the archipelago's main beach destination. Its star is Radhanagar Beach — Beach No. 7 — on the west coast, which holds Blue Flag certification for clean, safe and well-managed beaches.

The island is the hub of India's dive scene. Snorkellers head to Elephant Beach, and there are kayaking trips through mangrove creeks and underwater sea walks. Government ferries and private catamarans connect Swaraj Dweep with Sri Vijaya Puram and Shaheed Dweep. For all its fame, Radhanagar is largely quiet for most of the day.

items.body: Spend an afternoon and sunset at Radhanagar Beach.
Snorkel at Elephant Beach.
Learn to dive or take a fun dive.
Kayak through the mangrove creeks.
Try an underwater sea walk.

places.name: Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island)
places.summary: A slower, quieter island of beaches, reefs and a natural rock arch.
places.seoTitle: Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island): Beaches & Natural Bridge
places.seoDescription: Visit Shaheed Dweep (Neil Island): Bharatpur, Sitapur and Laxmanpur beaches, the natural rock arch, snorkelling and exploring by bicycle.

images.alt: A natural rock arch draped in greenery on the shore of Neil Island
images.caption: The natural bridge, Shaheed Dweep

overview.text:
Shaheed Dweep, formerly Neil Island, is the quieter neighbour of Swaraj Dweep — a place of small villages, slow days and very little traffic, where most of the food on the table is seafood caught the same morning. Its beaches each have their own character: Bharatpur and Sitapur for swimming and sunsets, and Laxmanpur, where a natural rock arch known locally as the 'Howrah Bridge' stands on the shore.

The island is small enough to explore by bicycle, and coral reefs just offshore make for good snorkelling and diving. Ferries link it with Sri Vijaya Puram and Swaraj Dweep.

items.body: The natural rock arch on Laxmanpur Beach.
Swimming and sunsets at Bharatpur and Sitapur.
Snorkelling over the reefs offshore.
Forest walks across the interior.
Seafood with Indian and South-East Asian flavours.

places.name: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park
places.summary: A 281.5 sq km marine park of 15 islands near Wandoor, protecting reefs and turtles.
places.seoTitle: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park: Jolly Buoy & Reefs
places.seoDescription: Visit the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park near Wandoor: Jolly Buoy and Red Skin islands, snorkelling, the no-plastic rule and opening days.

images.commons: File:Jolly Bouy Island, Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park.jpg
images.alt: Turquoise water and a white-sand island fringed with trees in the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park
images.caption: Jolly Buoy Island

overview.text:
Established in 1983, the Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park covers 281.5 sq km of sea, creeks and 15 islands near Wandoor, south-west of Sri Vijaya Puram. It protects fringing coral reefs, nesting sea turtles and other marine life; its islands fall into two groups, the Labyrinth Islands and the Twin Islands, and staff also help turtles injured in fishing nets.

Boats run to Jolly Buoy and Red Skin islands, which open to visitors alternately for six months each, for snorkelling over the reefs. The park is a strictly enforced no-plastic zone. Incredible India lists it as open 9 am–3 pm and closed on Mondays.

items.body: Nesting sea turtles at the Turtle Breeding Centre.
Snorkelling over fringing coral reefs.
Diving among schools of fish and rays.
Boat trips through the Labyrinth and Twin island groups.

itineraries.title: The Andaman Islands in 5 days
itineraries.summary: The Cellular Jail and Ross Island, two nights on Swaraj Dweep for Radhanagar and the reefs, a day on quiet Shaheed Dweep, and back via the capital.
itineraries.seoTitle: 5-Day Andaman Itinerary: Havelock, Neil & Port Blair
